art.subject: Besra (Accipiter virgatus), adult male: crown, nape and upperparts dark slate-grey, the head darkest; throat white with a bold black stripe down its centre; upper breast washed rufous, with only diffuse, narrow greyish shaft streaks; lower breast, belly, flanks and thighs broadly barred rufous-brown and white; undertail coverts white; tail grey-brown crossed by broad dark bars. Bill dark grey, short and hooked; legs and feet yellow, long and slender.
art.pose: perched upright on a shaded branch inside the forest, side view
art.scene: dense broadleaf forest on a southern Korean island in spring, dappled light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched upright on a shaded branch: dark slate-grey upperparts with the head darkest, white throat with a broad dark mesial stripe, underparts broadly barred rufous-brown and white, long tail crossed by 3–4 broad dark bands about as wide as the pale ones, short hooked bill, long slender yellow legs

adult male, in flight seen squarely from below: short, rounded wings spread straight out to the sides to their full span, whitish flight feathers crossed by broad dark bars, white throat with a dark mesial stripe, rufous-barred body, long tail with 3–4 broad dark bands, yellow feet tucked under the tail
art.build: Small, compact hawk, about the size of a Japanese Sparrowhawk or slightly larger, the female larger than the male. Head rounded, with no crest; the crown feathers lie flat. Neck short. Bill short and strongly hooked, much shorter than the head. Legs long and slender, yellow, with long thin toes. Wings short and rounded; flight a few rapid flaps followed by short glides, the underwing barred. Tail fairly long and square-tipped, crossed by broad dark bars.
avoid: Do not paint the plain, unbarred pale rufous breast and longer, more pointed wings of Japanese Sparrowhawk (Accipiter gularis); the adult male Besra is broadly barred rufous-brown below.
Do not leave out the bold black stripe down the centre of the white throat.
Do not add a crest on the nape; that is the much larger Crested Goshawk (Accipiter trivirgatus), which shares the throat stripe.
Do not paint bold dark teardrop streaks on a white breast or brown upperparts; those mark the female and juvenile, not this adult male.
Do not paint long, pointed falcon wings; the wings are short and rounded.
